name: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia with t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2)
aliases: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia with Philadelphia chromosome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: Presence of leukemic blasts expressing markers of more than one lineage (myeloid and lymphoid) confirmed by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry
Detection of t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2) translocation or BCR-ABL1 fusion gene by cytogenetics, FISH, or molecular methods
Bone marrow or peripheral blood blasts ≥20%
Exclusion of other acute leukemias such as pure acute lymphoblastic leukemia or acute myeloid leukemia without mixed phenotype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ≥20% blasts with biphenotypic marker expression and confirmed t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2) translocation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of immunophenotyping and cytogenetic/molecular findings.

searchTerms: immature white blood cells in blood
presence of leukemic blasts in circulation
cancer cells with specific genetic marker
pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells
petechiae and bruising from low platelets
recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells
low blood cell counts causing fatigue

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement
lung problems from blood cell buildup

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing blasts with mixed lineage markers
Positive BCR-ABL1 fusion gene by PCR
imaging: Chest X-ray may show leukostasis-related infiltrates
MRI or CT if CNS involvement suspected
other: Flow cytometry demonstrating biphenotypic antigen expression
Coagulation profile abnormalities in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly lymphoid lineage markers without myeloid expression
Similar t(9;22) but lacks biphenotypic expression
Predominantly myeloid lineage markers without lymphoid expression
Presence of t(9;22) but no mixed phenotype
Mixed lineage markers present but absence of Philadelphia chromosome

redFlags: Signs of leukostasis (e.g., respiratory distress, neurological symptoms)
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
